{{Short description|Fill device}}
The '''KIK-30''' "Really Simple Key loader" (RASKL) is a [[fill device]] made by [[Sypris Electronics]] and approved by the US [[National Security Agency]] for the distribution of NSA [[Type 1 product|Type 1]] cryptographic [[key (cryptography)|keys]]. It can also store and transfer related communications security material, including control data ("load sets") for [[frequency hopping]] radios, such as [[SINCGARS]] and [[Have Quick]].<ref>[https://www.sypriselectronics.com/information-security/global-key-management/raskl/RASKL(tm) KIK-30  The First Modernized KYK-13 Replacement]</ref> It can store up to 40 cryptographic keys and has male and female [[U-229]] connectors for the NSA DS-101 and 102 fill protocol, allowing it to be plugged into most other NSA fill devices and [[EKMS]] equipment. It is 6.14 inches (159 mm) long, weighs less than one pound (454 g) and is powered by four [[AAA battery|AAA batteries]]. The operator interface has an 8 line of 20 characters and 6 buttons, with what Sypris calls "1-button key squirt" and 2-button zeroize (clear memory).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sypriselectronics.com/media/5711/syp-19787-raskl-brochure.pdf|title = Electronic Manufacturing &#124; ECM &#124; Sypris Electronics}}</ref>

A simpler device than the [[AN/CYZ-10]], the KIK-30 is now planned to replace the venerable [[KYK-13]] fill devices, with up to $200 million budgeted in 2009 to procure the newer units in quantity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://defensesystems.com/articles/2009/11/12/dod-cryptographic-key.aspx|title=DOD modernizes cryptographic device -}}</ref>
